analysis.title: Credit Finally Cracks As Junk Bonds Suffer Biggest Blowout Of 2026
key_insights: US high yield spreads widened 51bps to 367bps last week, the biggest weekly widening of 2026 and about double the prior record of 27bps from late September. 1,753 of 1,934 index bonds lost value.
IG spreads widened 10bps to 96bps, but Treasuries rallied 24bps so IG yield fell 14bps to 5.87% and IG returned +0.84% on the week versus -0.86% for junk, the widest IG/HY return gap of 2026.

Cash bonds overshot equity beta while CDS indices undershot. Cash HY widened 51bps versus about 39bps implied by 4.5bps per 1% S&P drop, while CDX HY's weekly return was only a 1.1 standard deviation event.
A regression of CDX HY on VIX at 35.9 implies about 420bps versus a 385bps close. The 35bps gap is matched on only 1.4% of days since January 2025.
Stress is climbing the ratings ladder. 65 bonds from 37 issuers fell 5 points or more last week versus 24 the prior week, and 45 were single-B or double-B. 488 such collapses year to date.
Triple-C spreads are 1,174bps, widest since April 2025, and the CCC-BB gap is 953bps. The share of the junk market inside 200bps fell 12.4 points in a week to 44.5%.

Problem sectors are broadening: cable, building products, junk financials (Icahn, Navient, goeasy), education and packaged food. All 45 index industry groups fell. Consumer Chapter 11 volumes are at multi-year highs.

AI credit is weakening. CoreWeave's four junk notes are bid at 77-82 and hyperscaler 10-year spreads widened 12.9% on the week, up 138% YTD. IG tech trades 21bps wide of the index versus 21bps tight in May.
Shelofsky sees the hyperscaler move as beta, with 2x beta to IG and correlation of 0.93 versus 0.74. Biswas and Shelofsky lean tactically bullish, but Shelofsky says to sell any rally.
Record IG supply of $198B in November, including the $25.2B A- rated SpaceX GPU financing at 8.26% yield. About $300-320B of chip financing next year may crowd out plain high yield demand.

Biswas bull case: spreads back near 10-year median, positioning not stretched, flows holding, and December is the lowest issuance month. Trade is long iTraxx Main via receiver and payer spread options.
Goldman macro credit desk (Omer) recommends the opposite, a CDX IG Feb 65/80 payer spread funded by selling the 55 receiver. The author notes Goldman desks hold opposing views.
On a history back to 2007, HY at 367bps is at the 33rd percentile (median 431bps), IG at 96bps the 20th (median 129bps), loans the 12th, and only CCCs screen wide at the 92nd percentile.

Fundamentals are a risk: Goldman forecasts a 4% US HY default rate in 2027. Morgan Stanley sees 4.5% HY and 4.75% loans and cut HY to underweight. Hawkish FOMC minutes show most members wanting more hikes.
Author's conclusion follows O'Connor: selection over reach, build portfolios from the top of the quality stack, and skip junk despite a possible seasonal December bounce.

risk_factors: Cash credit liquidity is thin and risk appetite is the lowest in several years.
Stress spreading from CCC to single-B and double-B credits and across sectors.
Growth scare as equity selling extends beyond tech.
Hawkish Fed with most FOMC members wanting more hikes.
About $300-320B of AI chip financing crowding out high yield demand.
Rising defaults, with Chapter 11 volumes at multi-year highs in consumer sectors.
IG spreads breaking above 100bps, a Hartnett recession tell.
vol_and_positioning: S&P one-month implied vol went from about the 58th to the 98th percentile of its 10-year range in a week. CDX IG vol went from about the 32nd to the 74th.
VIX hit 35.9 and Goldman's Panic Index is 9.8 of 10. All 14 prior sessions with VIX above 30 since January 2025 had CDX HY at 404bps or wider, while CDX HY closed at 385bps.
Macro and systematic accounts bought CDX protection. Junk clients bought 1.5 to 1, mostly BBs and Bs. Dealers were net lifted on $1.3B of risk Friday.
Hartnett EPFR data shows $7.4B bond fund outflows, the first since April 2025. Lipper shows IG and EUR HY inflows.
Hedge funds dumped US financials at the fastest pace in five years per Goldman prime book.
Mutual funds and ETFs hold about half benchmark weight in junk data center bonds, and 67% of top 50 HY funds beat their benchmark.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley cut high yield to underweight in its 2027 outlook, with defaults at 4.5% in junk and 4.75% in loans.
Morgan Stanley went max overweight stocks.
BofA's Hartnett saw $7.4 billion leave bond funds, versus Lipper showing inflows.
Hartnett names IG spreads above 100bps as a recession tell and expects a relief bounce after Thanksgiving.
Morgan Stanley's Nick Savone warned weakest borrowers were telling a different story.

tension_points.bull_case: Biswas says valuations are back to the 10-year median, positioning is not stretched, flows are holding and December issuance is lowest, so a sustained widening is unlikely.
tension_points.bear_case: On a 2007 history junk is only at the 33rd percentile. Defaults are forecast at 4%, stress is climbing the ratings ladder, and $300B of chip financing competes for buyers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG spreads closing above 100bps, Hartnett's recession tell, or a growth scare spreading beyond tech.

tension_points.bull_case: Shelofsky sees the move as macro beta, with correlation to IG at 0.93, not an AI-specific problem.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler spreads are up 138% YTD and trade at 2x index beta, and GPU-backed paper offers HY-like yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler beta to IG normalizing toward the 1.5x average and spreads retracing.
